description: The grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the accuracy of various configurations, categorized by different layer types and perturbations. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled at an angle, and is organized into four distinct color-coded groups without an explicit axis title. The vertical axis represents "Accuracy" on a linear scale ranging from 70 to 95, with numeric tick labels at intervals of 5. Notably, the vertical axis includes a small grey shaded rectangle between the values of approximately 79.5 and 81. Each category on the horizontal axis corresponds to a pair of bars, where the left bar is a lighter shade and the right bar is a darker shade of the group's base color, and all bars feature a thin black outline. The first group consists of two blue pairs labeled "embedding" and "1st layer," with values ranging from approximately 80 to 82.2. The second group contains five green pairs ("random layers", "random layers +B₂", "random layers +L₂", "random layers +R₂", "random layers +permute"), where the lighter left bars measure around 79.4 to 79.7 and the darker right bars measure around 81.4 to 81.8. The third group comprises five red pairs ("random", "random +B₂", "random +L₂", "random +R₂", "random +permute") which represent the lowest values on the chart; the lighter left bars range from approximately 71.6 to 72.0, with the light red "random +R₂" bar being the shortest overall at roughly 71.6, while the darker right bars range from 73.1 to 73.5. The final category, "unperturbed," is represented by an orange pair and contains the tallest bars in the chart, with the light orange left bar at approximately 90.4 and the dark orange right bar reaching the maximum value of approximately 91.8. The bars are not sorted by height but are instead arranged categorically by their color groupings.
